name: discharged weapon (last year)
universe: Employed police officers and security guards in the United States
A: Police officer (sworn local, state, or federal)
N: Security guard (paid private security, all armed and unarmed)
C: Urban police officer: serves a jurisdiction with population >=400,000 or department in the central city of a metropolitan area
D: Rural/small-jurisdiction police officer: serves a community with population under 400,000 outside a major central city
T: Discharged a weapon in the last year: intentional on-duty firearm discharge in the past 12 months, excluding training and gun-range practice; accidental discharges excluded
sources: No national annual rate. MN BCA Uniform Crime Report 2023: 17 law-enforcement course-of-duty firearm discharges / 9,969 sworn MN officers ≈ 0.17%/year statewide; 2 private-security course-of-employment discharges (https://www.lrl.mn.gov/docs/2024/mandated/241258.pdf). Washington Post Fatal Force ~1,000 fatal police shootings/year nationally (~0.13%/officer-year) is a lower bound for discharges at a person. Urban/rural split extrapolated from Pew career urban/rural ratio. P(T|N) from MN security incidents ÷ BLS MN security employment.

name: CA Trump voter
A: Registered voter whose home state is California
N: Registered voter whose home state is not California
C: Other California registrant: lives in NorCal, Central Valley, or any CA county outside the SoCal list (non–Los Angeles, Orange, San Diego, Riverside, San Bernardino, Ventura, Imperial)
D: Southern California registrant: registered voter in Los Angeles, Orange, San Diego, Riverside, San Bernardino, Ventura, or Imperial counties
T: Voted for Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election (non-voters and other candidates count as T negative)
sources: State SOS active voter registration (CA ~22M / US ~160–180M). SoCal vs Other CA split from Census county population. 2024 presidential results by county (CA statewide Trump ~38% of ballots). P(T|·) among registrants = turnout × candidate share; P(T|N) from national non-CA weighted average. Trap: CA Trump vote share (~40%) is P(T|A) among voters, not P(A|T).

name: healthcare employment
A: Health care professional (clinical licensed or credentialed: physicians, nurses, PAs, pharmacists, therapists, etc.)
N: Employed adult who is not a health care professional
D: Non-physician health care professional among A (nurses, PAs, pharmacists, therapists, etc.)
T: Works in a hospital (NAICS 622 inpatient hospital; any job role)
sources: BLS Occupational Employment Statistics: healthcare practitioners + technical occupations; physicians ~1.1M. AMA/AAMC practice settings for P(T|C). BLS: majority of RNs employed in hospitals for P(T|D). Hospital employment ~5.9M / workforce ~160M for P(T). P(T|N): non-clinical hospital staff (admin, facilities, food) ÷ non-HCP workforce. Trap: P(hospital|physician) != P(physician|hospital).

name: military overseas (federal pool)
universe: US active-duty military plus US federal civilian employees
A: Active-duty US military service member (Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, or Coast Guard)
N: US federal civilian employee (executive-branch civil service, Foreign Service, and comparable federal civilian personnel; excludes active-duty military and USPS)
D: US Navy or US Air Force active-duty service member (Space Force grouped with Air Force; Marine Corps and Coast Guard unassigned in C/D split)
T: Has worked overseas: for military, at least one deployment or overseas assignment outside the 50 states since joining (RAND HRBS 'ever deployed'); for federal civilians, ever served in a substantial overseas posting (Foreign Service careers are essentially all-OCONUS; other federal series vary)
sources: P(A) ≈ 0.40: DMDC ~1.32M active duty / (~1.32M + OPM ~1.87M federal civilians on board). Military rates: RAND 2018 HRBS (60.4% ever deployed; Army 57.9%, Navy 71.7%, Air Force 55.0%). P(T|N) ≈ 0.08: blend Foreign Service ~14k at ~95% ever OCONUS (AFSA; excluded from OPM FedScope) with ~6% ever OCONUS among other federal civil service (estimate from DoD civilian rotation patterns). OPM FedScope: 21,393 / 1.87M ≈ 1.14% currently OCONUS (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/data-analysis-documentation/federal-employment-reports/reports-publications/federal-civilian-employment/). Current snapshot in this pool gives P(A|T) ~85% (P(T|N) ≈ 0.011). Trap: using national employed universe (P(A) ≈ 0.8%) instead of federal pool reverses the posterior to ~10%.

name: covid vaccine (blue/red)
A: Received the updated 2024-25 COVID-19 vaccine: at least one dose since August 2024 (2024-25 season shot; matches Pew/KFF/CDC seasonal wording)
N: Did not receive the updated 2024-25 COVID-19 vaccine (includes never-vaccinated and people vaccinated in prior seasons only)
C: Blue-state resident among A: lives in a state won by Biden in the 2020 presidential election (state-level; NE/ME district splits ignored)
D: Red-state resident among A: lives in a state won by Trump in 2020
T: Had COVID-19 in the past 12 months: positive test (rapid, PCR, or home) or provider diagnosis; reinfections count as T positive
sources: P(A) = 0.27: Pew March 2025 -- 27% of adults got updated COVID vaccine since Aug 2024 (https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/03/20/more-americans-report-getting-a-flu-shot-than-the-updated-covid-19-vaccine-since-august/); KFF ~23% full 2024-25 season; CDC NIS-FRVM 17.9% by Nov 9 2024 (MMWR 73(46)). P(C|A), P(D|A): blue states ~55% of US population with ~30% seasonal uptake vs red ~45% at ~15% (CDC jurisdiction range VT 33.9% vs PR 5.2%; partisan geography literature). P(T|·): no national survey ties seasonal vaccine status to past-12-month infection directly; P(T|N) ~0.13 from NHIS ever-infected rise 2023-2024 (~6 pp/year) plus reinfections, calibrated so P(T|A) < P(T|N) with modest VE against infection (NEJM veterans 2024-25 outcome VE ~20-37%). P(T|C), P(T|D) extrapolated from geographic case/death divides post-vaccine (ABC/AP analyses). Trap: P(A|T) ~27% if you answer with P(A); ~73% if you use 1-P(A) without Bayes; most vaccinated live in blue states but most COVID cases are among the unvaccinated majority.

name: NAEP grade 4 reading (MA vs NM)
universe: Public school fourth graders in Massachusetts or New Mexico
A: Public school fourth grader in Massachusetts or New Mexico (entire universe)
N: Not applicable outside this universe (placeholder; P(A)=1)
D: New Mexico public school fourth grader
T: Proficient reader: at or above NAEP Proficient on the 2024 grade-4 reading assessment (same national assessment and achievement-level definition in both states)
sources: Universe restricted to the MA–NM pair. Enrollment fall 2022 CCD (Table 203.40): MA 66,751 + NM 22,503 = 89,254 fourth graders; P(C|A)=66,751/89,254≈0.748, P(D|A)=22,503/89,254≈0.252. P(T|C)=0.40, P(T|D)=0.20: 2024 NAEP reading snapshots (https://nces.ed.gov/nationsreportcard/subject/publications/stt2024/pdf/2024220MA4.pdf, https://nces.ed.gov/nationsreportcard/subject/publications/stt2024/pdf/2024220NM4.pdf). P(MA|T)=0.40×0.748/(0.40×0.748+0.20×0.252)≈0.856. Trap: P(T|MA)=40% or P(MA)=75% alone are not P(MA|T)≈86%.

name: HS graduation ACGR (WV vs AZ)
universe: Public school twelfth graders in West Virginia or Arizona
A: Public school twelfth grader in West Virginia or Arizona (entire universe)
N: Not applicable outside this universe (placeholder; P(A)=1)
C: West Virginia public school twelfth grader
T: On-time graduate: graduated within four years with a regular high school diploma under the federal adjusted cohort graduation rate (ACGR; same national methodology in both states)
sources: Universe restricted to the WV–AZ pair. Grade-12 enrollment fall 2022 CCD (Table 203.40): WV 17,489 + AZ 95,122 = 112,611 twelfth graders; P(C|A)=17,489/112,611≈0.155, P(D|A)=95,122/112,611≈0.845. P(T|C)=0.91, P(T|D)=0.76: 2021–22 ACGR, NCES Digest Table 219.46 (https://nces.ed.gov/programs/digest/d23/tables/dt23_219.46.asp). P(WV|T)=0.91×0.155/(0.91×0.155+0.76×0.845)≈0.180. Trap: P(T|WV)=91% or P(WV)=15.5% alone are not P(WV|T)≈18%; Arizona’s much larger cohort pulls the posterior down despite a lower rate.

name: fantasy sports (male vs female)
N: Not applicable outside this universe (placeholder; P(A)=1)
T: Played fantasy sports for money in the past year (NCPG: season-long or daily fantasy with entry fees)
sources: Universe = all US adults. P(C|A)=0.49 male and P(D|A)=0.51 female (Census sex share of adults). P(T)=0.24 past-year fantasy sports for money; players are 70% male / 30% female (NCPG NGAGE 2.0 2021). P(T|C)=0.70×0.24/0.49≈0.34; P(T|D)=0.30×0.24/0.51≈0.14. P(male|fantasy)=0.34×0.49/(0.34×0.49+0.14×0.51)=0.70 (matches NCPG composition). Trap: P(T|male)=34% or 50/50 base rate are not P(male|T)=70%.

name: physician vs PhD research
universe: US-residing active physicians plus US-residing employed research doctorate holders in any science, engineering, or health field (NSF SDR 2023)
A: Member of this combined workforce (entire universe)
N: Not applicable outside this universe (placeholder; P(A)=1)
C: Physician (MD/DO) in this workforce; includes MD-PhD dual-degree holders
D: Research doctorate holder without an MD in this workforce (NSF SDR; excludes MD/DO)
T: Engaged in research as part of professional work: among physicians AAMC NSSP 2022 self-reported research engagement; among PhD holders NSF SDR 2023 primary work activity is research and development
sources: Universe ≈1.03M active physicians (AAMC 2024) + ≈867K employed research doctorates without MD (SDR 2023: 908,700 employed SEH doctorates minus ~41K MD-PhD overlap at ~4% of physicians). P(C|A)=1,032,365/1,899,765≈0.54. P(T|C)=0.14: NSSP 2022 (JAMA Netw Open 2024; doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.33140). P(T|D)=0.39: SDR 2023 primary activity R&D among all employed doctorates (355,450/908,700; NSF 25-321 tab015-002). T definitions differ slightly (self-reported engagement vs primary R&D activity) — harmonize before shipping. P(T|A)≈0.25; P(MD|T)≈30%. Trap: answer 14% (P(research|MD)) or 54% (MD share) instead of ~30%. Alternative T=practice medicine fails: P(T|MD)≈0.84 direct patient care (AAMC 2024) but P(T|PhD)≈0, so P(MD|practices)≈99% — no interesting inverse-confusion.

name: tax MFJ single CTC
universe: US individual income tax returns filed as married filing jointly or single (tax year 2021; IRS SOI Publication 1304)
A: Return in this filing-status pair (entire universe)
N: Not applicable outside this universe (placeholder; P(A)=1)
T: Claimed at least one qualifying child for the Child Tax Credit (proxy: primary recipient of an advance Child Tax Credit payment in 2021; filing status from TY 2019/2020 return used for eligibility)
sources: Universe restricted to MFJ or single (excludes head of household, MFS, QSS). P(C|A)=54,161,246/(54,161,246+81,422,759)=0.40 from Pub 1304 TY 2021 return counts. P(T|C)=19,481,385/54,161,246≈0.36; P(T|D)=2,432,327/81,422,759≈0.03 from IRS SOI advance CTC Table 3 (2021 cumulative). Head-of-household filers excluded because most unmarried parents with children use HOH. Trap: answer 36% (P(CTC|MFJ)) or 40% (MFJ share) instead of P(MFJ|CTC)≈89%.

name: homeownership under 35 vs 65
universe: US occupied housing units where householder is under age 35 or age 65 or older (ACS 2024 1-year)
A: Household in this age pair (entire universe)
N: Not applicable outside this universe (placeholder; P(A)=1)
T: Owner-occupied housing unit (householder owns or is buying the home)
sources: Universe restricted to under-35 or 65+ householders (middle ages excluded). ACS 2024 1-year Table B25007: under-35 occupied units=25,366,954 (owners=8,982,014); 65+=37,604,725 (owners=29,565,704). P(C|A)=25.37M/62.97M≈0.40. P(T|C)=8.98M/25.37M≈0.35; P(T|D)=29.57M/37.60M≈0.79. P(under 35|T)≈23%. Trap: answer 35% (P(owner|young)) or 40% (young share) instead of ~23%. ACS Housing report 2023 reports 36.1% and 78.5% for same age bands (2023 vintage).
